The working file is the complete analysis; the Markdown/PDF reports are reader copies of it. Each should be read in full — this message is only a pointer, not the analysis.

In brief: the recommendation (confidence MEDIUM) is **not** to build an open-ended free tier. "Free tier is low-cost" is directly contradicted by Finance's own cost-scaling fact, and "competitors have one so we need one" turns out to be an analogy about their funnel fit, not evidence about this company's. A locked-weight trade-off across six criteria (cost-risk, cannibalization, motion fit, signal quality, reversibility, competitive parity) ranks a **land-and-expand refinement of the existing outbound motion** highest, robust to any single weight change — ahead of full freemium, freemium-lite, a plain trial, or a usage-based entry tier. Layered on top, as a cheap and reversible way to close the one real gap (no internal conversion/cost data exists), the analysis recommends a **small, sales-gated, time-boxed trial pilot** — justified by a separate Fermi estimate showing the unit economics are genuinely undetermined (not clearly favorable or unfavorable) without that data. The report names four concrete conditions that would flip this (verified low per-user cost, favorable pilot data, documented lost deals tied to the lack of a free tier, or a deliberate shift toward a self-serve-native segment).
